subject: Lodestar pilot throughput & headroom sizing request
messages:
From: Samir Rao <samir@lodestar.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-15T09:12:00Z
Subject: Pilot sizing request: tokens/sec target + SLO constraints

Hi Jonas,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the throughput numbers looked promising. We are lining up a 3-month pilot and need a realistic sizing estimate to take to our infrastructure and procurement teams. High level:

- Traffic profile: ~120k daily active users at launch, spike windows during business hours (14:00-18:00 PT).
- Typical prompt/response length: client prompts ~40 tokens, model responses ~180 tokens (avg 220 tokens per call).
- Expected steady-state concurrent QPS (calls/sec): avg 35, peak 200 for short bursts (90th pct burst windows).
- Target SLO: p95 end-to-end generation latency <= 1.2s for chat flows.
- We would prefer a dedicated pool (reserved capacity) for isolation and predictability.

Ask: can you provide a tokens/sec / GPU mapping for a recommended Dedicated configuration (including suggested conservative headroom for traffic growth + warm cache assumptions)? Also include fallback guidance (e.g. smaller quantized model variants) if committed capacity is insufficient during peaks.

I can loop procurement (procurement@lodestar.ai) if you need a PO cadence. Would like a short writeup + spreadsheet so I can share with our ops folks.

Best,
Samir Rao
Head of Platform, Lodestar AI
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Samir Rao <samir@lodestar.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-16T14:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Pilot sizing request: tokens/sec target + SLO constraints

Samir — great to hear. Quick read of your profile: with 220 tokens/call, peak 200 calls/sec -> 44k tokens/sec peak. For Dedicated sizing we'll translate tokens/sec into GPU slab sizing using our inference throughput baselines.

Initial assumptions I used:
- Model: 13B transformer (baseline we demoed) quantized to int8 performance profile.
- Measured baseline (no KV cache): ~9k tokens/sec per A100-equivalent GPU under low latency configuration.
- With prefix/KV warm cache and continuous batching tuned for your burst shape, effective tokens/sec per GPU improves ~25% during steady bursts.

Quick back-of-envelope:
- Peak tokens/sec: 44,000 -> Raw GPUs needed (no headroom): 44,000 / 11,250 (cached throughput) ≈ 3.9 -> 4 GPUs.
- Recommended committed slab: 6 GPUs (this gives ~50% headroom to absorb 2x short bursts and mitigate noisy neighbor effects + maintenance windows).
- If you want tighter p95 (<=1.2s) across variable request sizes, plan for 8 GPUs for predictable latency headroom when cold caches or heavier prompts hit.

Fallbacks / cost-control levers:
- Fallback model variant (6B quantized): 1.8x tokens/sec per GPU but measured degradation in longer-coherence outputs; use for non-critical background flows.
- Dynamic burst routing: keep a small hosted pool (on-demand) to absorb unexpected 3-5x spikes.

I'll attach a short spreadsheet with throughput math and assumptions. Kimberly — can you confirm whether we should model 20% tail overhead for multi-turn KV growth? Marissa — can you draft a simple MA POC SLA table for the committed 6 vs 8 GPU options?

Next steps: I will send the sizing spreadsheet and a short narrative for procurement, and propose a follow-up call Thurs to align.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Director, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference
From: Lina Wu <lina.wu@lodestar.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Rao <samir@lodestar.ai>, procurement@lodestar.ai
Date: 2026-10-18T10:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Pilot sizing request: tokens/sec target + SLO constraints

Jonas — thanks for the quick turnaround. A couple of follow-ups from ops/procurement:

- For internal budgeting, can you break out estimated monthly token cost vs reserved GPU capacity cost for the 6 GPU and 8 GPU options? We will likely ask finance for a committed monthly run rate.
- Our flows include occasional multi-turn chains where the KV cache can grow to ~1,200 tokens per session (not just prompt + response). Please include a sensitivity line for KV growth that reduces cached throughput by ~15-25%.
- Procurement: we need a simple list of proposed SLAs (p95 latency, availability, credit policy) for the pilot window. PO turnaround is ~2 weeks once we have the numbers.

Attaching our internal traffic sample and a brief runbook.

Regards,
Lina Wu
Product Ops, Lodestar AI
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Lina Wu <lina.wu@lodestar.ai>, Samir Rao <samir@lodestar.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, procurement@lodestar.ai
Date: 2026-10-20T16:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Pilot sizing request: tokens/sec target + SLO constraints

Lina / Samir — attached is the requested spreadsheet (lodestar_sizing_estimate_v1.xlsx) and a 1-page service matrix (lodestar_service_matrix.pdf). Summary of the sizing analysis and commercial implications below.

Executive summary:
- Measured baseline (13B int8) with warmed KV cache: ~11.25k tokens/sec per A100-equivalent GPU. Without KV warm cache: ~9k tokens/sec.
- Peak tokens/sec (your profile): 44k. Mapped GPU needs:
  - Conservative committed option (6 GPUs): supports ~67.5k tokens/sec cached capacity; expected p95 latency ~1.0-1.3s under normal bursts. Includes ~50% headroom for short growth and maintenance.
  - Robust committed option (8 GPUs): supports ~90k tokens/sec cached capacity; expected p95 latency ~0.8-1.0s and stronger resilience to cold-cache events.

Sensitivity to KV growth / multi-turn:
- If KV grows to an avg 1,200 tokens/session, cached throughput drops ~20% -> effective cached tokens/sec per GPU ≈ 9k. Under that scenario:
  - 6 GPUs -> effective capacity ~54k tokens/sec (still above your 44k peak, reduced headroom).
  - 8 GPUs -> effective capacity ~72k tokens/sec (comfortably above peak).

Cost and billing notes (estimates for pilot month):
- Reserved GPU monthly fee: estimated in spreadsheet (line items for 6 GPU and 8 GPU slabs).
- Token billing (hosted fallback usage) separated; we recommend keeping a small on-demand hosted pool to avoid hard throttles during unexpected spikes.

SLA sketch for pilot:
- Availability: 99.9% for Dedicated pool (monthly).
- Latency: target p95 <=1.2s for committed config; SLA credits for sustained p95 >1.4s measured over 24h window.
- Support: 24/7 incident escalation for Dedicated customers on enterprise plan.

Recommendations / next steps:
1) For launch-to-production pilot, commit to 6 GPUs and include a triggered scale path to 8 GPUs if daily 7-day moving peak approaches >70% of committed capacity.
2) Enable KV pre-warm for key autopredict flows to maintain cached throughput.
3) Configure dynamic fallback rules to route non-critical flows to quantized 6B variant during 3-5x unexpected spikes.
4) Procurement: we'll draft a short-term pilot addendum (30–90 days) with PO line items.

Kimberly and Marissa will follow up with an MA POC SLA table and a procurement-ready quote. Happy to jump on a call Thurs 10/21 to walk through the spreadsheet.

Regards,
Jonas Weber
Director, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference
